# `pos sale` commands

## `pos sale complete`

Complete a POS sale: posts the sales receipt `sales-receipt post` would, through the same core, with the facts the register fixes (its deposit account, its site, today's date, the chosen customer or its walk-in, a payment method it offers), and records the ticket, register, clerk and tender. One payment method: cash takes at least the total and returns the change; any other method takes the total, with an optional reference. expected_total is the total shown (pos sale preview); a different total posts nothing (E_PREVIEW_STALE). The ticket key is the operation key: completing again with the same key returns the sale already posted and never posts twice. An agent records sales with `sales-receipt post`. Needs pos.sell; a typed unit_price also pos.price-override. Off unless company setting pos_enabled is on (E_FEATURE_DISABLED).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | member pos.sell; pos.price-override when a line has unit_price |
| Capability | pos.sell |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pos.sale.complete` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow pos sale complete --ticket 01JPOSEXAMPLETICKET0000001 --lines '[{"item":"Pipe Sealant","quantity":"2"}]' --tender '{"payment_method":"Cash","amount":"20"}' --expected-total 16.08 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pos sale complete", "input": {"ticket": "01JPOSEXAMPLETICKET0000001", "lines": [{"item": "Pipe Sealant", "quantity": "2"}], "tender": {"payment_method": "Cash", "amount": "20"}, "expected_total": "16.08"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pos_register` | `--pos-register` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Register ID or name; omitted when the company has one. |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer ID or name, from `pos customer search` or `add`. Omitted, the sale is the register's walk-in customer's, which the POS screen and the receipt never show. |
| `lines[].item` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Item ID or name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `lines[].quantity` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string | no | no | "1" | Quantity, in the item base unit; default 1. |
| `lines[].unit_price` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | A typed unit price, overriding the register's price (needs pos.price-override). Omitted, the price is the sales receipt's own: the item price, the customer's price level and the price rules. |
| `lines[].serial_numbers` | inside `--lines` JSON array | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Serial numbers of the units sold, for a serial-tracked item; omitted, the units stay unassigned, as the sales receipt allows. |
| `ticket_version` | `--ticket-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Required version for a resumed held ticket. |
| `ticket` | `--ticket` | string | yes | no | — | The ticket's key, chosen by the device when the sale starts (a ULID or any 1-64 letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-'). It is the sale's operation key: completing again with the same key returns the sale already posted and never posts a second.; pattern "^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$" |
| `tender.payment_method` | `--tender-payment-method` | string | yes | no | — | One of the payment methods the register offers (ID or name).; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `tender.amount` | `--tender-amount` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Amount tendered. For cash, at least the total (the change is the difference); for any other method it is the total, the default. |
| `tender.reference` | `--tender-reference` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Card or check reference (last four digits, approval code), stored as the receipt's payment reference. |
| `expected_total` | `--expected-total` | string | yes | no | — | `pos sale preview`'s total, which the clerk saw. If the sale now totals anything else (a price changed meanwhile), nothing posts and E_PREVIEW_STALE carries the new total.; minimum length 1; maximum length 32; pattern "^\\d+(\\.\\d{1,2})?$" |

## `pos sale preview`

The exact totals of a cart, as `sales-receipt post`'s dry run gives them: the lines as they will post (price levels, price rules, discounts and subtotals resolved), tax and total, for the chosen customer or the register's walk-in (null on screen). Writes nothing. A typed unit_price needs pos.price-override. Needs pos.sell. Off unless company setting pos_enabled is on (E_FEATURE_DISABLED).

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member pos.sell; pos.price-override when a line has unit_price |
| Capability | pos.sell |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pos.sale.preview` |
| External binary body | none |

## `pos sale void`

Void a completed POS sale through the same reversal as sales-receipt void, with a required context reason and receipt expected_version. The sale selector accepts the POS sale ID, ticket key, receipt ID or number; an ordinary typed receipt is refused. Keeps the original receipt and immutable reversal history. A deposited sale is refused naming its deposit; a reconciled sale is refused. A sale with a POS refund is refused naming the refund. Needs pos.void, not pos.sell or ledger.post. Off unless company setting pos_enabled is on (E_FEATURE_DISABLED).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | member pos.void |
| Capability | pos.void |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pos.sale.void` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow pos sale void counter-cart-1 --expected-version 1 --reason "Customer canceled" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pos sale void", "input": {"sale": "counter-cart-1", "expected_version": 1}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sale` | `SALE` | string | yes | no | — | POS sale ID, ticket key, sales receipt ID or receipt number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | The current sales receipt version; a newly completed sale is version 1.; minimum 1 |

| `ticket` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `id` | string | yes | no | — | Sales receipt ID. |
| `number` | string | yes | no | — | Sales receipt number. |
| `status` | literal["voided"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `version` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `changed` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "changed": false,
  "dry_run": false,
  "id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "number": "value",
  "sale_id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "status": "voided",
  "ticket": "value",
  "version": 1,
  "warnings": []
}
```

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DEPOSIT_DEPENDENCY` | The receipt is claimed by a deposit; an atomic coordinated correction is required. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERIOD_CLOSED` | An affected accounting date is in a closed period. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECONCILIATION_DEPENDENCY` | Another reconciliation record depends on the one this change would move. |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
| `E_WORK_DEPENDENCY` | The accepted or linked work prevents this change; inspect the related document. |
